in writing. i believe it is important to create an independent and accountable fundamental rights agency. a balance must be struck between these two requirements, keeping in mind that the main thing is to design a functional and efficient organ. to achieve this objective, active and close cooperation between the three european institutions is essential. the first thing to do is to find a political consensus. the council has indicated that it does not want the competence of the european agency for fundamental rights to be extended to the third pillar, i.e. intergovernmental cooperation in the fields of police, justice, immigration and counter-terrorism. the netherlands even announced that it would use its veto to prevent the agency from starting its activities on 1 january 2007 because of the duplication of work with the council of europe. that is why, while i voted unanimously in favour of all the amendments to mrs kinga gál's report, i voted in favour of postponing the final vote so that the council can reconsider its position.
in writing. according to the report: "the fundamental rights agency should be an adequate body to provide regular review of the application of human rights". the future agency will therefore have to study the increasing number of violations of freedom of expression in europe. unfortunately, there are many examples: the cartoons of muhammad published in a danish newspaper, which have led to the death of priests in turkey, violent demonstrations and the burning of churches, the speech of pope benedict xvi which was considered "hateful and hostile" by a turkish muslim leader, and, more recently, the french philosopher redeker who was threatened with death and forced to change his address every day for a text on the koran whose content is prejudicial and offensive to the prophet, islam and muslims. self-censorship, threats and attacks are increasing at the expense of freedom of expression and thought, to the point that today they are probably the most threatened freedoms in europe. so if the first task of this future agency is to defend these freedoms and to denounce the violations, we are in favour of it. if not, it will be yet another useless and costly theodule committee.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my excellent colleague, mr jan christian ehler, on the follow-up to the report on competition in the professions. however, i abstained on certain provisions relating to advertising, as there was no precise information on the impact of the communication on the professional and ethical quality of the services provided and on the price of the services. i share the view that it is essential to integrate the professions into our european internal market, but we must take account of their specificities in connection with the special and indispensable protection of the european consumer in a highly internationalised market for services. beyond these considerations, it seems to me absolutely essential to ensure that the liberal professions are given greater recognition within the european political institutions and have their full place in the logic of the social market economy in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of the excellent report by my colleague and friend daniel varela suanzes-carpegna on economic and trade relations between the european union and mercosur. i am grateful to him, in particular, for his willingness to accept amendments concerning the place of small and mediumsized enterprises in the cooperation part of the association agreement with mercosur and the financing to be attached to it, as well as the role of the organisations representing smes. at a time when negotiations at the world trade organisation are failing and the european union is going to negotiate bilateral agreements, this report sets out the way forward for trade cooperation with this very important part of the american continent. if the association agreement could be finalised, the free trade area thus created would be the largest between regions in the world and would open up major opportunities for trade and, therefore, for economic growth on both sides, while improving the international competitiveness of both markets.
in writing. although the european union is defending itself against this, it is intensifying bilateral trade negotiations to compensate for the foreseeable failure of the doha round of negotiations. and these negotiations have the same defects as those of the wto: the concessions of the european union to its partners are much greater than the concessions of the partners to the eu; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. some of the mercosur member states already benefit from the european union's generalised system of preferences, i.e. duty-free and quota-free access to the european market. the question is, what are the mutual interests of the future trading partners, since the costs of a 'no-deal' represent a small part of the volume of trade between the two parties. the main objective of this agreement seems to be the vanity of having created the world's first interregional free trade area, soon to be extended to the entire american continent. this is yet another example of brussels' tendency to put ideological objectives ahead of all other considerations, especially economic and social ones.

it is clear that the recovery of community funds following irregularities or fraud remains insufficient. the financial regulation must be applied more strictly and its revision must be carried out. the parliament therefore considers that simplification of recovery procedures and better coordination between the commission services and those responsible at national level are essential areas of work. the main problem is that no single national authority has overall responsibility for the quality and supervision of national controls, while 80% of the implementation of the community budget is the responsibility of the member states, as a result of shared management. the complexity of the mechanisms thus leads the media to blame the commission for the problems associated with illegal operations, and thus for the recovery of the money, whereas these problems are primarily at the level of the member states. strengthening cooperation between olaf, eurojust and europol, a wider application of the judicial recovery procedure and parliament's request that the commission provide a regulatory framework for the accounting treatment of irregularities and that it regularly report, by dg, on the state of recovery are all important measures that will increase the transparency and efficiency of the procedures.

madam president, in france, breast cancer is first diagnosed by mammography, and then confirmed by anatomical pathology. we'd need to check for extension to the liver, brain and bone, which are the three targets of metastasis. at best, in france, we'll only do a bone scan, but no mri and especially no pepscan, a device for early metabolic diagnosis. in treatment, if there is radiation therapy, it is a humble manipulator who will do the deeds. the result is sometimes peripheral radiation accidents to the heart or thyroid. finally, if after treatment, when checking the patient with back pain, a scan is obtained that shows a suspicious bone spot, pepscan screening is still not done. why would you do that? because in france, for every 35 million women, there are only two pepscans. why would you do that? because the budget covenant prohibits spending on hospital equipment. the result is that women in europe are dying not only of breast cancer but also of the ideological cancer of the european commission, which is called fiscal malthusianism and wild free trade.
madam president, commissioner, breast cancer kills too many women in the european union, and often far too young women. these deaths are unacceptable when we know that early detection can cure this cancer. we know the psychological and physical trauma that women experience when they discover their disease: they have to reorganize their family and professional lives and simply cope. there is no harmonisation in europe on how to deal with the scourge of breast cancer. only ten member states are carrying out screening, with varying degrees of success. european women are therefore faced with a situation of blatant inequality, because they live in a particular country or city. commissioner, our objective is to eradicate this disease, knowing that in addition to the trauma experienced by the patient, this disease has a cost to our society. the solution to this scourge is early and compulsory screening, organised by the governments of the member states. to be effective, this testing must be free of charge and, above all, well-managed, which means that state-of-the-art equipment must be available throughout the european union. digital mammography, which in the past could hide microcalcifications - the most common lesions of breast cancer - has made considerable progress. so, commissioner, when will we have digital mammograms throughout the european union? effective screening also requires that all devices are calibrated and therefore quality checked, knowing that nothing is more serious than the false security given to women by an x-ray examination that may be of poor quality. to make this test effective, equipment alone is not enough. doctors who are called upon to make these diagnoses must undergo continuing training. they must undergo continuous retraining and compulsory tests to assess their knowledge. finally, women need information on breast cancer prevention, advice on lifestyle and food hygiene and no fear of screening. research should help us to make progress on the causes of breast cancer. i am convinced that by pooling our efforts we can once again explain what the european union is doing to improve the health of european women. this is a subject on which there should be unanimity in the european union: zero deaths from breast cancer in europe!
madam president, commissioners, first of all i would like to thank my colleagues for their work and for the clarity of their statements. the problem we are looking at today is a serious one. the alarming statistics on the spread of breast cancer in europe and the number of deaths from the disease are sufficient to prove this. this problem is all the more serious given the very wide disparities between countries in both cancer prevention and cancer treatment, which have become even more pronounced since the last enlargement. while the treaties provide that the european union, together with the member states, is to work to protect and promote the health of european citizens, the word 'jointly' will nevertheless have to be given a stronger meaning. the eu guidelines and recommendations have not been sufficiently taken into account. we must now act against this situation and not tolerate it any longer. the european union must ensure that its citizens have equal access to detection, management and the best available treatment. to this end we have the legislative and budgetary instruments, as well as the structural funds and research programmes. let us use all the resources we have to look at all the causes of this disease, whether environmental, social or genetic, and to look for innovative treatments. the commission must make proposals to this effect and i sincerely believe that the european union should make the fight against breast cancer and, more generally, the fight against cancer in general, a priority policy, knowing that together we will always be stronger. this is the added value that our citizens expect from the european union. studies and diagnoses, evaluations and resolutions are necessary but action is crucial. the commission and the council must therefore hear our warning and waste no more time.

in writing. the schengen information system (sis) is a police cooperation instrument which aims to centralise and facilitate the exchange of information on wanted persons, objects or vehicles between police services in the member states. some 13 million pieces of information are stored in the current system. we are being asked to create a second generation of sis, sis ii, which would be extended to the new member states. we cannot adhere to it. nor have we joined schengen i, which provides for the free movement of persons by removing the internal frontiers of the member states. the problem is not to have a supercomputer that can list all the people or property wanted by the police, but to ensure that each national territory can be a safe area. the mass immigration that is sweeping the european coastlines every day proves that it is the frontiers that must be protected, that they are the real gateways to insecurity and illegality. all the computers in the world could thus collect as much personal data as possible, but the fact remains that the main source of the problems of insecurity, trafficking of all kinds and illegal immigration is the lack of effective control of the internal and external borders of the european union.

my dear colleagues, what a mess! the few citizens who are interested in our debates will hardly understand why a debate on pollution in côte d'ivoire is being mixed up this afternoon with another on a case law that upsets the principle of subsidiarity. the fact that the judgment of 13 september 2005 was delivered on an environmental directive does not change that. its wording is in fact a judgment in principle on the communitization of criminal law. this is a real constitutional revolution, because we know that at least nine other areas of competence are being absorbed, without a treaty, by the european union, including criminal immigration law and intellectual property law. yes, there is pollution, ladies and gentlemen, there is a real judicial pollution of the european treaties by the luxembourg court! in this confused and ill-founded judgment there is no textual reference and no clear case-law principle. vague, ill-defined and over-drawn considerations of expediency lead to his hasty and sloppy conclusion. the mechanics are familiar. the vague conclusions command the indefinite extension of the competences of the european union, then justify the interpretation of the commission, which finally legitimizes the transfer of powers from the states to the court. those who, like us, were wary of the substantial enlargement of the union's objectives in article 103 of the draft constitution were quite right. the commissioners and the judges are not prepared to bow to the will of the people and are determined to ignore the refusal to ratify a draft constitution which was precisely the one which was passing criminal matters through the ordinary community legislative procedure. this judgment distorts the will of those who signed and ratified the european treaties. this is a legal coup. we are on the verge of important deadlines. our people are watching us and will soon hold us accountable. will there be any sincere democrats here to reject this blue dictatorship?

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, first of all i would like to thank all my colleagues, and in particular barbara weiler and werner langen, with whom we have done a wonderful job. let us hope that the text will be voted on tomorrow. it is simply a question of securing the exercise of subsidiarity for tools, ppps, which are very familiar to our local authorities, and have been for many, many years. i welcome the commission's intention to legislate on concessions, which have been confused with public procurement for too long. but, as i say here, i believe that we also need to legislate on institutional public-private partnerships. it is wrong to say that these are new forms: mixed-economy companies have existed since 1955 in france and stadtwerke for a very long time in germany. but today, to subject them to double competition is to condemn them. what private partner would agree to work with a local authority that puts it in competition a second time? i would also draw the commissioner's attention to the danger of inter-municipal structures, which are liable to be confused with private structures, when they are a wholly public form of organisation for small municipalities which are striving to be large enough to cope with increasingly demanding public service obligations and tasks.
commissioner, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the barbara weiler report provides the clarity and readability we needed on public-private partnerships, which makes it possible to correct the errors of the european court of justice and to improve legal clarity for all those involved. concessions are too often confused with public procurement: the latter involve the purchase of goods for consumption by the local authority, whereas concessions give the public authority the possibility of delegating the performance of part of its tasks to a third party. so yes to legislation on these concessions and not just to an interpretative communication. the same applies to institutionalized ppps. their creation is currently threatened by the rigors of the case law which tends to double competition for the award of works, which would seal the fate of mixed economy companies. so i thank our rapporteur for calling for a legislative initiative on this subject. finally, in the commission v spain judgment, the intermunicipal structure became a private partner for the court of justice. a municipality should therefore compete with an intermunicipal structure to which it delegates service provision. mrs weiler is restoring the rule of law and is giving us the best parliamentary contribution on this subject, and i thank her for that.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we must recognize the real existence of a european labour market, particularly in the service sector, which, more than any other, involves the displacement of workers. we are in favour of this, but not on any conditions and not at the risk of social dumping. human labour is not a commodity and cannot be subject to the rules of free competition. we expressed this concern during the debate on the services directive and parliament rejected - you recalled - articles 24 and 25 of that directive, which deal specifically with the relaxation of the conditions for the posting of workers. it is unacceptable that the commission should question this position and ignore the criticisms made by parliament. the directive on the posting of workers is poorly applied in the member states and does not meet its objectives. but should the rules be relaxed or, on the contrary, should the will to enforce them be strengthened? i do not believe that reporting requirements, effective controls and the preservation of records create an unnecessary bureaucratic burden when it comes to protecting the social rights of posted and local workers. the only people who benefit from laxity in this area are the fraudsters. in addition, the strengthening of the enforcement and the threat of financial sanctions must act as a deterrent. i therefore support this report and urge the commission and the member states to resolve the difficulties in implementing the directive, which we are not at this stage calling for to be amended.
the rapporteur. mr president, mr president of the european central bank, ladies and gentlemen, the annual report of the central bank always provides the european parliament with an opportunity to take stock of monetary policy and to supplement the work of the economic and monetary affairs committee through the monetary dialogue that we hold four times a year with the president of the central bank. we all remember that last year we rejected this report, which did not correspond to the guidelines that this parliament wanted. the year 2005 is a special year in which the central bank initiated a movement of five interest rate hikes, the first of which was on 1 december. these successive increases are taking place in a particular economic context, determined both by the rise in oil prices, by an exchange rate unfavourable to euro area exports and in the context of a recovery in economic growth which the most informed observers consider to be fragile. in these circumstances, this report calls on the central bank to analyse carefully the conditions under which it conducts its monetary policy. the report also stresses - and i welcome this - the importance of the euro-dollar parity for growth in the european union and draws a number of conclusions from it, which have been drawn up in a spirit of compromise, taking into account the need for each monetary authority to exercise its responsibilities in the field of exchange rates fully. i hope that compromise will still exist at the time of the vote. i would nevertheless like to express some regret that it is not possible in this report to address both the question of household indebtedness and the need to improve the coordination of economic policies. let me mention a number of points, mr president, on which i believe this report makes an original contribution. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the euro is not used as a currency. but let us now come to the essential points for this parliament, namely the conditions under which democratic control is exercised and the way in which the central bank functions as an institution. in this respect, we wanted to contribute, before the next renewal of a member of the executive board, to the necessary debate which must be opened up between the institutions so that the members of the executive board can represent the interests of the euro area in the best possible way. we believe that to this end the ecb should be treated in the same way as other central banks, i.e. with a diversity of profiles and a balanced portfolio. we are in agreement in this parliament that the balance between nations should not be regarded as an eternal status quo and we also believe that the diversity of profiles should enrich the contributions and the plurality of the executive board. i also hope that this parliament will advocate that the council, when it decides to validate an appointment to the executive board, should exercise its full the euro area should allow for this plurality of candidates. of course, we are also asking for the european parliament to finally be empowered to approve the appointment of the members of the executive board, which i believe would only strengthen the authority of the said members of the executive board, their legitimacy and their capacity to embody a strong voice for the euro area, including on the international scene. that is the whole purpose of this parliament, namely that the central bank should be, on the international scene, alongside the council and the eurogroup, the major and legitimate interlocutor we need to make europe's voice heard on such important subjects as those which you, mr president, have been pleased to address and on which this parliament wishes to make its contribution. i am thinking of course of the alternative funds, on which i hope that the compromise we have worked out in the committee on economic and monetary affairs will be supported by in writing. the european parliament adopted the 2007 budget of the european union at first reading on thursday 26 october. the 120 billion euro is the first year of the new financial perspective for 2007-13, which was adopted last may and which the french socialists did not approve, believing that it does not allow them to meet the major challenges of the future. in this context, the 2007 budget is very modest, corresponding to a level of 1.04% of the gni of the european union. the many internal and international constraints on the european union have led parliament to identify priorities which should help citizens to better perceive the union's added value. the socialists therefore decided to vote on this 2007 budget after obtaining satisfaction on their priorities linked to the lisbon and gothenburg strategies. this is particularly the case for education, training, research and sustainable development. the renewal of the communication policy and the emergence of new pilot projects are also positive for the future of the european union.
in writing. this vote is part of an unacceptable multiannual budgetary framework. a detailed examination of the budget lines shows that there is a glaring lack of funds in many areas such as research, innovation, major technological projects such as galileo and the major transeuropean networks. this budget will not encourage the recovery of growth in europe. european aid to the countries of the south, to africa and the maghreb is years away from a development policy which, however, should be implemented urgently to deal with the imbalances in migration and poverty. it is urgent to create a european tax guaranteeing a high level of own resources for a european budget that is finally up to the challenge!
in writing. the european parliament voted today, under the urgency procedure, a council regulation on the management of fishing fleets registered in the outermost regions, which extends the current regulation for one year. the main derogations allowed relate to the entry of fishing vessels into the fleet, public aid for the renewal of vessels and aid for modernisation. this regulation takes account of the situation of the fisheries sector in the outermost regions, which still has a great potential for development and abundant fisheries resources. it would therefore be unthinkable and counterproductive to prevent the fishing fleets of these regions from benefiting from such facilities! i hope that the overseas fishermen will take advantage of these new deadlines to develop and modernise their fleets. i regret, however, that the european commission has not yet suggested any longer-term orientation. i have already asked on many occasions for these derogations to be extended beyond 2006. it would have been better to accept this proposal from the outset rather than to ask our parliament every year to extend to the following year derogations which are in any case essential for the fisheries of our regions!

in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the community legal framework for public-private partnerships (ppp) does indeed need clarification. but this clarification must respect a number of principles, in particular: it must actually concern only public-private partnerships, be based on a distinction between partnerships/markets on the one hand and partnerships/concessions on the other, respect the specificities of the partnerships/markets and therefore renounce any new specific regulation of ppps, not call into question the rule of the negotiated procedure applied to concessions, respect the freedom of choice of organisation (creation of mixed-economy companies or other legal forms, takeover of a private company by a public structure, outsourcing, etc.) of the national public authorities, and finally ensure that any community initiative is consistent with the public service imperatives and national choices in this area. all this is unlikely to require the adoption of new binding legal acts. since the european union's intervention in these matters seems inevitable, let us at least make sure that it does not lead to the development of one of those bureaucratic machinations of which brussels-based europe is the secret.
in writing. the rapporteur rightly wants to counteract the european commission's unfortunately chronic liberal drift. it is unacceptable that in its communication the commission has attempted to reintroduce the principle of country of origin, which was rejected by the european parliament when it voted on the services directive. i agree with the rapporteur who calls for strict application and control of this directive as soon as possible and for the introduction of financial penalties. the commission must accept the case law of the court of justice, which distinguishes between selfemployed and posted workers and ensures the most favourable social standard for the latter.
in writing. it is a fact: the directive on the posting of workers, which is poorly applied in some member states, does not meet its objectives. this is due to differences in the interpretation of some key concepts (worker, minimum wage and subcontracting), the difficulties in monitoring compliance with the directive and in accessing information, both for workers and smes. an effective system of cooperation between member states requires a stronger involvement of the social partners, the provision of information to posted workers on their respective rights and the contact points for enterprises, in particular smes and craft enterprises. finally, it is now imperative that the european commission examine constructive solutions to prevent and eliminate unfair competition, as exemplified by letterbox companies or double posting from one state to another, as well as social dumping resulting from the abusive posting of workers, in particular through the 'fake self-employed'. the aim is not to change the acquis of the directive, but to improve it. that is why i voted in favour of mrs schroedter's own-initiative report.

in writing. with the introduction of the euro 7 years ago, the purchasing power of europeans has decreased considerably. in the eurozone there was indeed a rise in prices for everyday and leisure consumption, and an even more pronounced trend in real estate due to a lack of supervision of hedge funds. thus, not to mention the over-indebtedness, the lower and middle classes are the hardest hit. economic growth in the eurozone has even slowed. in fact, gdp by volume increased from +1.8% in 2004 to +1.4% in 2005. the outlook for 2007-13 is even more worrying, as the euro will put european growth at risk a little more as soon as the exchange rate becomes too favourable against the dollar. not only does this bank with its europeanist foundations and philosophy have a democratic deficit and a certain lack of transparency, but none of the economic and social objectives of the european union will be achieved. these indicators should convey the message that we must leave the euro zone and that nations must regain their powers over economic, social and monetary decisions in a free europe where national and community protection and preference will come first.

member of the commission. mr president, the commission fully shares the concerns expressed by the honourable members of parliament regarding the recent shooting by china’s people’s liberation army of tibetan refugees at the border between the people’s republic of china and nepal, the subsequent death of one of them and the imprisonment of some of those refugees. the matter has been formally taken up by the european union in the framework of the last session of the eu-china human rights dialogue, held in beijing on 19 october, as rightly mentioned by the honourable member from finland. on that occasion, the european union refuted the claim by china that the shooting had been in self-defence, urged the chinese government to undertake a thorough investigation of the incident and insisted that the imprisoned refugees be treated in compliance with international humanitarian standards. more generally, the commission is very concerned about the human rights situation in tibet, and in particular the preservation of the cultural, religious and linguistic identity of the tibetan people. this issue has been regularly addressed during the bilateral dialogue on human rights as well as at the highest level, during bilateral summits. the european union is particularly concerned about the number of tibetans from religious backgrounds who are in prison for political reasons, and has repeatedly asked for their immediate release. several of these people are on the list of individual cases regularly submitted to the chinese authorities on the margins of these dialogues. the commission believes that china’s policy in tibet is not consistent with the provisions of the international covenant on civil and political rights. the early ratification by china of this covenant ranks among the top priorities of the european union in the field of human rights and we have left china in no doubt as to the need to fully respect the spirit of that covenant, once it has been signed and even before it is ratified. as part of its overall policy vis-à-vis tibet, the european union has consistently taken the view that establishing a direct dialogue between the dalai lama and the chinese authorities is the only realistic way to find a peaceful and lasting solution to the question of tibet. we have therefore welcomed and closely monitored the five rounds of talks so far held between the special envoys of the dalai lama and the chinese government. the commission urges both sides to continue this dialogue and use these talks to try to make substantive progress.

have been condemned by the osce office for democratic institutions and human rights as patently unfair. subsequent developments also give little ground for optimism. torture is reported to remain widespread. no international body has been able to obtain access to refugees returned to uzbekistan. uzbekistan refuses to cooperate with united nations special procedures. civil society and human rights defenders are subject to constant harassment. indeed, many human rights defenders have been imprisoned. the commission has noted with particular concern that several prominent human rights activists have been sentenced to several years’ imprisonment, while mukhtabar todjibaeva remains in detention. we are aware of many similar cases. despite this bleak picture, nothing is to be gained by cutting off all channels of communication with uzbekistan. as honourable members are aware, in response to the andijan killings, the european union adopted sanctions against uzbekistan, namely as mentioned here earlier, an arms embargo, a travel ban for those individuals responsible for the andijan killings and the suspension of technical meetings with uzbekistan. a decision whether to prolong or extend the scope of these sanctions must be taken by 14 november. in order to enable member states to obtain a full and comprehensive picture of the situation in uzbekistan, a cooperation council will be held with uzbekistan at the beginning of november. moreover, this cooperation council will provide an opportunity for the european union to raise directly with the uzbek authorities, at ministerial level, our many concerns on andijan and its aftermath. in the light of this cooperation council, the member states will take their decision on the possible prolongation or extension of the sanctions.

mr president, an unprecedented power outage struck western europe on the night of 4 to 5 november. it reveals the fragility of the european energy system and the lack of electricity generation and transmission capacity, the result of a poor investment policy. despite the risk of blackouts, european operators have been reducing their investment levels for the past six years, from 16 to 10% of their turnover. at the same time, electricity consumption has been steadily increasing by 1.8% per year. this decline in investment is a direct consequence of the liberalisation of the energy market. rather than investing in the development of new production capacity, operators concentrate their efforts on profits and buying up their competitors. citizens are seeing the rise in electricity prices on the one hand and the decline in security on the other. only a european energy policy could guarantee good cooperation between member states and the necessary investments of around €700 billion by 2030. electricity is a public good: this must be reflected in political initiatives of the european union.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, i welcome the opportunity this plenary debate offers us to take stock together of the functioning of the euro area at a time when, as you said, certain prospects are improving, but when, also, everyone is aware that the growth potential is not being fully exploited and when our economies are handicapped by an exchange rate which makes it difficult for euro area exports and is leading some of our companies to consider relocating to produce in the dollar zone. this report provides an opportunity to take stock at a time when the stability pact has been revised and everyone is aware that the commitments made by the euro area member states may need to be better differentiated from those made outside the area. in this respect, the report is useful and i think we should also congratulate mr garcía-margallo on the spirit in which he has dealt with it. we need to go beyond the reform of the stability pact to better coordinate timetables and data, to verify that, in essence, the commission and the central bank do not assess the performance of the euro area member states solely in terms of their deficits, but also in terms of their strengths and weaknesses in a more global context. you mentioned this in your speech, commissioner, and i thank you for it. i would urge you to continue along this path. the macroeconomic analysis will also have to be better aligned with developments on financial markets. the way in which the rating agencies have been able to take an interest in the italian question and assess the debt of that country should also encourage us to be more vigilant, because there would be a very serious risk from the point of view of the management of the euro area if the rating agencies were to take a leading role in the assessment of the debts of the member states. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this report contains a number of interesting and welcome recommendations. i would like to thank the rapporteur for that. so instead of calling for only a reduction in public expenditure, it is a question of freeing up resources for what are supposedly necessary public investments in education, training, infrastructure and research. the european parliament, too, instead of recommending wage moderation, admits - that is the term used - that in the long term real wages and productivity should grow at the same rate. i thank the rapporteur for these efforts at moderation and conciliation. but the subject of this debate is the economic state of the euro area. i believe that despite the recent and even unexpected improvement in growth indicators, the economic situation remains fragile and unsatisfactory. the commission's macroeconomic policy affects the daily lives of millions of european citizens whose purchasing power is threatened by stagnating wages and rising living costs and worsening working conditions. social protection is also weakening. the practical response of the commission and the central bank is always the same: to combat inflation by means of budgetary austerity and wage moderation, on the one hand, and to increase competition in the market for services, capital, products and labour, on the other. perhaps it is time to take stock of the results of this policy and ask whether the dismantling of public services, the deregulation of the labour market, the reduction of public spending, are really sustainable engines of growth in the euro area and in the european union. unfortunately, no pause for thought is on the agenda. in two days' time we shall have to decide on a directive on services which has been improved but which is still faithful to the deregulatory inspiration of fritz bolkestein. in a few months' time, a directive proposing the end of the public postal service will be on the agenda. as for energy, despite the chronic instability of oil-producing areas, despite the gas blackmail of a neighbouring country, despite global warming, despite widespread power cuts in half of europe, nothing is done, the answer is still the same: complete the liberalised and deregulated internal energy market in europe. the economic report of the euro area is perhaps a little better this year; i think that the social and political record of the commission is still as bad as it was.
although the report by my distinguished colleague, mr josé manuel garcia-margallo y marfil, contains some very interesting analyses and proposals on the euro area, i regret that it does not raise the question of the evolution of the euro from a technical currency to a political instrument for growth and employment. the monetary policy of the european central bank (ecb) appears to be the opposite of reality: normally the exchange rate should be strong when economic growth is strong and should depreciate when growth is weak. in europe, however, the opposite has been happening since the early 1990s. while member states are reforming, the pursuit of zero inflation through inappropriate monetary policy is leading europe to record poor economic growth performance. if this continues, as the price of raw materials and energy soars across the planet, we will have zero inflation and zero growth with manufacturers eventually settling in the dollar zone. it is as if the ecb were ignorant of economic policy, while its american counterpart is only concerned with economic policy.
the rapporteur. mr commissioner, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all, as rapporteur, let me thank the non-attached rapporteurs from the various groups and the committee on the environment, public health and food safety for their willingness to support a collective effort to improve the commission's proposal. as you said, commissioner, the seas and oceans of our planet are in a worrying state: a level of alert has been reached. in fact, a recent study published in science warned of the danger of fish stocks in our seas and oceans being depleted. the quality of the marine ecosystem plays a fundamental role in the overall environment of the planet and, in particular, a very important regulatory role in the climate. our seas also play a crucial role in the life of the entire planet. as you have said, they play a major economic role: fishing, transport, tourism, sources of raw materials and, finally, activities along the coast. but our seas and oceans are under increasing pressure and worrying pollution. first of all, let us remember this figure: 80% of marine pollution comes from land and as you said, commissioner, it is obvious that there is a direct link between the water framework directive and the directive you have presented and which our parliament wishes to improve. but if pollution comes from the land through water, it also comes through the atmosphere. recent studies show a large interaction between atmospheric movements, air pollution and the sea and oceans, so that urbanization and human activities occurring far from the coast can have a direct impact on water quality. pollution is also generated by activities related to the exploitation of the oceans and seas, such as transport and aquaculture. the waste from fishing and oil activities reached, in some sectors, quite excessive and dangerous levels a few years ago. we are also at a time when new threats are emerging which the directive must anticipate. in particular, we are seeing a proliferation of desalination projects for seawater. it is necessary to ensure that these activities do not lead to a deterioration in the quality of water in the future. there is a great deal of international debate about carbon dioxide storage. so you see, the threats are very real. the directive has tried to put in place an architecture which will finally enable us to have a strategy that goes beyond the international conventions, the results of which have so far, for the most part, not lived up to expectations. our directive is based on the first point: the restoration of the good ecological condition of the seas. parliament wants, commissioner, that the obligation to deliver results should be much more present, much stronger than the text as it stands now. secondly, our parliament wants the good ecological status of the seas and oceans to be defined much more precisely so that it is not a wishful thinking and that we come as close as possible to what can be done to restore life and balance to the ecosystem. thirdly, our parliament wants the deadlines to be shorter and in any case to strike a good balance between the deadlines, the level of environmental requirements and the obligation to deliver results. finally, we are in favour of the creation of marine protected areas, because the us and new zealand experiences have shown that these protected areas - and in some cases, these genuine marine reserves - are capable of restoring fish stocks. finally, we want territorial cohesion to be strengthened by good work at the level of the marine and sub-marine regions, without however relieving the member states of their responsibilities in relation to the objectives set by the management plans and the plans for measures to restore good ecological status. we are anxious to include the black sea in the document. we want to sound the alarm about the arctic: we must think about the future of this part of the world which is directly linked to us and whose evolution has considerable implications for the future of the planet, which may be threatened. we want the outermost regions of the union, which are not yet included in the document, to be gradually included in a suitable strategy. i will end with the democratic issues. we see this every day: whether it is fishing or transport, sea users, environmentalists, scientists feel the need to confront their points of view so that the decisions that will be taken are based on a shared diagnosis and a rational analysis of the problems. that is the spirit of the amendments we have tabled.
on behalf of the alde group. thank you for your communication. it is imperative that a thorough and rigorous investigation be carried out into the causes of the power cuts which have affected many countries of the european union. is this a failure of information? what, for not following procedure? a network failure? a lack of investment? was it a fault in the maintenance of the network or a commercial cause? some european citizens see this failure as a negative consequence of energy liberalisation, others see it as a failure of interconnections and the transeuropean energy network. as you have pointed out, the management of this blackout can also be seen as a demonstration of the solidarity of the member states with germany, which is without electricity, and as the discharge procedures were put in place to avoid the much more serious consequences of a european blackout. if the failure is of a commercial nature, the regulators of the member states should jointly define and review the applicable rules to better control the electricity market. if the failure is of a technical nature or due to a procedural defect, then better coordination is needed between the energy transmission system operators, as they are the operational links of smooth and secure energy exchanges. the creation of a european energy networks centre would make it possible to establish a european network code to harmonise the standards and procedures of the member states' networks. in conclusion, i welcome the fact that the commission has launched this inquiry and i hope, let me stress, that it will communicate the results in full transparency so that we can make progress in avoiding any such incidents.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank our rapporteur, mr jan mulder, for his constant work, not only on budgetary questions in general but also on questions concerning the financing of agricultural and rural policies. the fact that i, as the permanent rapporteur on the structural funds in my committee, have asked to speak in this debate on the modification of the ceilings for development support from the eafrd is to express two things. firstly, it is a 'democratic' regret, but also a 'strategic' wish. i very much regret that the european parliament is being forced to change ceilings which it has already adopted, in order to bring them into line with decisions taken by the council. in addition, my 'strategic' wish is to reiterate our commitment to the fundamental principles of rural development policy, primarily because they give europe a sense of readability. i would like us to remain very cautious in the face of the temptation to generalize compulsory cofinancing which could lead in the long run to a renationalization of expenditure under the first pillar. such a decision should not be the subject of a policy of "water on the water" but should be considered as an important issue to be subjected to a clear and democratic debate. as for the necessary - and perhaps justified - christmas 'gifts' given in portugal, i regret that there is no real strategy on this subject and i ask that we define one and that it be the result of a substantive debate.
mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, everyone knows about the 2003 reform of the cap, which provided for the freezing of the first pillar and the strengthening of the second, namely rural development. the agreement on the new financial perspective - which i voted against - runs counter to both of these commitments. the rural development envelope has lost €20 billion compared to the commission's proposal, which is 35% less for the 15 former member states than in the current period. the proposal for voluntary additional modulation of up to 20% of the amounts from the first to the second pillar, which does not meet any of the criteria applicable to rural development policy, is not acceptable. i recognize that the european commission has tried in its proposal for a regulation to frame this tool, but i share the rapporteur's concerns and support his proposal for rejection: there is indeed too much risk of distortion of competition if some states choose to take 20% of direct aid and not others. it is unacceptable that this voluntary modulation is not subject to the same rules as those normally applied to rural development, and the risk of renationalisation of the cap is too great. on the other hand, the financing needs of rural development policy are real and i fear that the desertification of our rural areas will increase. i therefore ask the commission to propose, instead of voluntary modulation, an identical increase in the compulsory rate of modulation in all member states. i would also like to point out that the compulsory modulation applies for the time being as soon as a holding receives more than eur 5 000 of agricultural aid per year. the vast majority of farms are affected. in order to have a real tool for redistributing aid, other criteria should also be taken into account, such as the size of the holding, its dependence on aid, the labour employed, the standard gross margin, etc. in addition, in order to ensure a fair distribution of agricultural aid, a ceiling on direct aid should be envisaged.
in its annual report, the court of auditors gives a positive statement of assurance on the 2005 accounts of the european union and congratulates the commission on the implementation of the new accounting system for the financial year. however, as regards the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions concerning the receipts received and the payments made, the court notes that appropriate risk management is still not guaranteed in important areas of expenditure. most of these errors are the result of ignorance of the applicable rules, ineligible expenditure or attempted fraud by the final beneficiaries (farmers, local authorities or project managers). who is to blame? firstly, the commission, which is directly responsible for implementing the european budget under the treaties. it must improve the quality of internal control, and procedures must be simplified to avoid non-compliance with the eligibility criteria, double-charging or overestimation of costs. finally, the states must also assume their responsibilities, since 76% of the funds are spent by national or local administrations. the commitment of the member states to provide annual reports on how the european union funds they manage are spent seems to me to be paramount.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my distinguished colleague, marie-hélène descamps, on the proposal for a european council decision on the agreement between the european union and canada establishing a framework for cooperation in the fields of higher education, training and youth. this report is in line with a long tradition of cooperation and it is only logical that we should have special links through our young people in the european union and canada, who are the sons of europe.
in writing. these agreements aim to strengthen our cooperation in the fields of higher education and training with canada and the united states. they renew, for a period of eight years from 2006 to 2013 , the cooperation programmes previously concluded with the european union in 1995 and 2000. the cooperation agreement negotiated with canada aims to strengthen and broaden the scope of the previous agreement by providing a new framework for cooperation in the field of youth. the new agreement with the united states, which partially renews the previous programme, introduces innovative programmes leading to transatlantic degrees. it aims to promote student and teacher exchanges, to strengthen the schuman-fulbright programme and to encourage closer institutional collaboration in higher education. both of these covenants have proved useful in the past. their implementation should improve the openness and competitiveness of our higher education systems for the future, while promoting mutual understanding and bringing our peoples closer together. i am glad that our parliament has voted in favour of their conclusion, thus strengthening the relations between our two continents.
in writing. i welcome the adoption at first reading of the report by mrs lienemann on the marine environment strategy directive, a key directive which forms part of the continuity of the water framework directive (wfd). i would like to express my scepticism, however, about the feasibility of the timetable which has just been adopted. the knowledge of the marine environment is not yet sufficient to make an effective assessment of the environmental situation of european seas in a short time. the preparation/conditioning phase is always difficult and takes longer than expected. in addition, the marine environment has a particularly high inertia. i therefore believe that the timetable proposed by the commission is already ambitious enough.
in writing. at a time when the union is facing a resurgence of national selfishness, the commission's proposal to introduce optional modulation of direct payments under the cap marks a new stage in the breakdown of community solidarity. in the face of this danger, parliament had to react and make its voice heard, in order to reaffirm the commitment of the representatives of the peoples of europe to defending the 'common' character of the union's public policies, of which the cap is the most striking symbol and the most successful achievement. i therefore voted in favour of the goeppel report which was tabled today in plenary, and in particular the explicit request that the european commission's proposal be rejected outright. this position, which expresses the opinion of the majority of members present today, reflects the clear and unambiguous will of the european parliament not to betray its vision of the future of europe, and not to make the cap a variable of adjustment designed to make up for the weaknesses of a european budget which is hampered by the lack of ambition of the member states of the union. it calls for the maintenance of a system of aid to producers, based on the principle of equity, which alone can guarantee the survival of a viable, competitive and united european agriculture in the future.

in writing. twenty-five national laws on mortgage lending and soon twenty-seven that run counter to a common european approach. this green paper proposed by the european commission will make it possible to carry out adequate studies on this issue and to take the right options. any community measure concerning the european mortgage credit market must first and foremost benefit the citizens directly, and consumers often face too many legal and economic obstacles. in voting in favour of mr john purvis' report, i have chosen to make the mortgage market accessible to a wider range of potential borrowers. i had personally insisted in the committee on the internal market that its rapporteur, mr medina ortega, take account of borrowers with a low and precarious credit profile, workers with fixed-term contracts and people making their first purchase.
president of the commission. mr president, honourable members, ladies and gentlemen, when the lights went out across europe last week, our interdependence as europeans was laid bare for all to see. in a flash, greater integration ceased to be some abstract ideal. for millions of our citizens, it became a necessity. the incident – dare i say it – was illuminating. the argument for more europe has not so much been won, as rendered superfluous. it is now clear to everyone that we face more shared challenges than ever before – thanks in part to the forces unleashed by globalisation. and shared challenges demand shared solutions, whether they relate to growth and jobs in an increasingly competitive world, climate change, energy security or, indeed, international terrorism. we can be proud of our response so far to this rapidly changing landscape. first, we renewed the lisbon agenda and placed the emphasis squarely on growth and jobs. as a result, it was possible to restore confidence in the stability and growth pact, putting it on a more realistic and workable footing. europe’s leaders agreed to put globalisation at the centre of its policy agenda, and the commission has been busy equipping the european union with the tools it needs, and using those tools, on a whole range of concerns that european citizens share. to boost growth and jobs, the european institutions have continued work to unleash the full potential of the single market. at the same time, we have renewed our commitment to social solidarity, including the setting-up of the globalisation adjustment fund, a useful shock absorber for the powerful motor of globalisation. to ensure that europe thrives in the knowledge economies of tomorrow, innovation became a central part of our economic and social strategies and today innovation is at the core of the concerns of european leaders. the establishment of the european institute of technology will help reverse the fragmentation of research, education and innovation efforts, which has stunted progress so far. the document ‘europe in the world’ tackles the need to develop a global voice which matches our economic weight in the world. this will also reinforce our efforts in areas where we have already exerted leadership, notably in the debate on a future international climate change regime. and we have successfully steered romania and bulgaria towards european union membership. we have proposed the two new commissioners and allocated the portfolios. one will be responsible for consumer affairs and the other for multilingualism, to protect and to reinforce european cultural pluralism and diversity. intercultural aspects are more and more important in the europe of today. i am very proud that this further step – romania and bulgaria joining the union – has taken place and that my commission has made an important contribution to it. i think we should all be very proud of what has been achieved through successive enlargements. let there be no doubt: in centuries to come, historians will say that enlargement was the greatest instrument for peace, prosperity and stability of our generation. (applause)on that note, i would like to say it is more than time we stopped talking about ‘old’ and ‘new’ member states. more than ever before, we are now one europe, united in all our diversity, and that is something we should celebrate. we have also laid the groundwork in many other areas that concern us all – sustainable development, maritime policy, and energy efficiency, to name just a few. we still have much to achieve by the end of this year. i hope that the european council will approve the enlargement package we adopted last week. we need to move forward on immigration and innovation policy and we still have important proposals to adopt in areas like labour law, copyright levies, neighbourhood policy, co2 emissions from cars and emissions trading. so the first years of this commission, working in a spirit of partnership with this parliament, have meant renewing, reorienting and re-tooling, to create a europe of results, a europe fit to face the shared challenges of the 21st century. these efforts are already bearing fruit: growth has been revised upwards to its highest level in six years; unemployment has dropped to its lowest level since we started collecting eu25 data in 1998. now 2007 – the year we celebrate 50 years of european construction – will mark a turning point. it will mark the moment when a europe of 27, after careful preparation, throws the full weight of the union’s re-tuned machinery behind the delivery of solutions to our citizens’ shared concerns. it will mark the moment when a new budgetary framework unlocks modernised financing programmes, which move towards europe’s new agenda. so this is the context for our 2007 work programme. it is a new type of programme that has greatly benefited from input from this parliament, the council and the other institutions: valuable input that will continue with this debate and the resolution you adopt. this work programme addresses many of parliament’s concerns that have been conveyed to me and to the commission. this new work programme is more political. it is focused on a smaller list of 21 strategic initiatives. the commission is committed to delivering all of these next year, and they will not be subject to a mid-term review. a second list of priority initiatives fills out our work in other important areas. in addition, we have responded to calls from parliament to include a list of simplification measures and withdrawals of legislative proposals in the work programme. this underlines the message that better regulation is now an integral part of the commission’s day-to-day tasks. today, in the college meeting, we adopted our strategic review of better regulation that takes stock of progress to date and sets out an ambitious programme of new initiatives. this includes new action in the following areas: impact assessment, where we will establish an impact assessment board; simplification, where we will add important new initiatives to our rolling programme; and administrative burdens, where we will suggest a target to the spring european council next year to cut such burdens at european union and member state levels by 25% by 2012. in parallel, we will present an action plan in two months’ time defining priority areas for action. we are also continuing to screen, and in a number of cases withdraw, pending proposals. we are recommending that future commissions do the same at the beginning of their mandates as an expression of the changed political composition of a new commission, so showing the importance of political legitimacy and political leadership. this review responds to a very large extent to the priorities of the european parliament, as expressed in several reports earlier this year. i hope you will give your full endorsement to this package, including to its practical implementation. so what does the 2007 work programme feature? let me highlight some key areas, those i believe to be politically very sensitive. first, energy. building on our green paper and measures for greater energy efficiency earlier this year, we will present the first ever strategic energy review for europe. this will include the building blocks for an integrated european union energy policy, for example measures to complete the internal market for electricity and gas; to accelerate take-up of new low-carbon technologies; and to diversify and secure supplies both within and outside europe. the goal is a common european energy policy that will ensure our security of supply, while maintaining europe’s competitiveness and safeguarding our environmental objectives. closely linked to this – in fact i could say they are two parts of the same agenda – will be action on climate change. we will put forward options for a european union climate change policy and perspectives for international cooperation post-kyoto. a revision of the european union emissions trading scheme will provide greater stability for investments and accelerate the momentum to cut greenhouse gases. europe’s demographic squeeze calls for greater efforts to attract economic migrants, particularly those who are skilled. a european regime for labour immigration will give such migrants a secure legal status, while clarifying their obligations and their rights. in order to reduce illegal immigration and exploitation of workers, this will be coupled with a clampdown on unscrupulous employers of third-country nationals who enter europe illegally. european public policy can have a fundamental impact on the way people live their lives. to be effective, it must be properly attuned to the needs of modern society. the commission will undertake a fundamental stocktaking of european society, which will serve as a basis for european policy-making into the next decade. as i have said several times, europe is more than a market. europe without the concept of solidarity is not really a european union. (applause) our core business, in terms of our competences under the treaties, will not be forgotten either. the commission will continue to defend, extend and modernise the single market. a key target for 2007 will be the defence industries and markets, which have been fragmented for far too long. we will also set out the way forward on services of general interest in the coming weeks. a final area of concern to all our citizens is security. the commission will bring forward additional measures to combat terrorism, with a particular focus on fighting terrorist propaganda and the sharing of expertise – on explosives for example – for terrorist purposes. the year 2007 will also mark a turning point in our search for an institutional settlement. the berlin declaration, marking the 50th anniversary of the treaty of rome, will allow europe’s leaders to renew their commitment to an enlarged, global and competitive europe, where solidarity is a central principle. i believe it should be a short, sharp political declaration, affirming what unites us and – above all – making clear where we want to go and what we want europe to be for the next 50 years. following my initial proposal, i am happy to see that everything is now moving in the direction of having a joint statement, a statement by the member states, the european commission and the european parliament, thus showing that the commitment to the european union is today a shared commitment of the main political institutions of our union. i am pleased to see that the search for an institutional settlement is also a priority for the german presidency. so i am confident that the elements are in place for an important breakthrough. this is important, because europe needs an institutional settlement. there are indeed serious costs derived from not having a constitutional treaty. we need the constitutional treaty because, as a european union, we need to be more effective in our decision-making, more coherent in our external action and more transparent and democratic in our working. make no mistake: the commission will be an active player in the search for solutions here. when this commission took office, there perspectives; we now have the revised stability and growth pact. in fact i hope tomorrow we can say we will have the revised services directive, to be approved by a parliamentary vote. that shows that we are solving some of the planning problems and proposals. it has been hard work, but it is already bearing fruit. the 2007 work programme builds on these new foundations. so we can conclude the work on decisions that were already in the pipeline but also launch new, very important, projects for the work of europe, such as energy policy. for the first time we have the chance to have a real common approach to energy, to be more ambitious in the fight against climate change, to look at the entire field of justice and at the fight against illegal migration. this is a new frontier for europe and we need to take a european approach. so we see that europe is on the move. there are problems. we know the problems that exist, but there are great possibilities and there is, more than ever, the need itself for the 21st century. to show our commitment to practical results and to working hard for a stronger european union, this can be a fitting birthday present for the 50th anniversary of europe, a birthday present for europe and all its citizens. president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the council is aware that iceland has announced that it will resume commercial whaling despite the moratorium on whaling by the international whaling commission (iwc) which has been in force since 1984. this was discussed at the environment council on 23 october under the agenda item 'other matters'. on 10 october 2002, iceland re-accepted the 1946 international convention for the regulation of whaling, but it raised a reservation with regard to the whaling moratorium. as the honourable member knows, membership of the international whaling commission is open to any country which is officially party to the 1946 convention. each member state may decide to accede to an international agreement covering matters which do not fall within the exclusive competence of the community. at present, 18 member states of the european union have acceded to the convention and are also members of the international whaling commission. the community is committed to the protection of whales as laid down in the habitats directive. the directive provides for a high level of whale protection, while prohibiting all intentional catching and killing of whales in community waters. furthermore, the importation of whale meat and other whale products into the community for mainly commercial purposes is strictly restricted by council regulation no 338 of 1997. following iceland's announcement of the resumption of commercial whaling, 15 eu member states of the international whaling commission and the european commission, together with australia, the united states and eight other like-minded countries, made an official appeal to reykjavik, urging iceland to comply with the moratorium and to end commercial whaling activities.

losses, without having similar protection for foreign players. as guardian of the treaty, the commission will examine all complaints that it receives. however, at the same time i do not underestimate the sensitivities that exist in many member states on the question of gambling. member states are fully entitled to protect general interest objectives, such as the protection of consumers. however there was a time when all mankind spoke one language and used the same words. but the bible account of the tower of babel episode relates that men tried to build a tower that would reach to the heavens and make them equal with god. to thwart this plan, god multiplied languages so that humans would no longer understand one another and would be scattered over the earth. with this report on multilingualism, europe is implementing an 'anti-babel tower' project, as it intends to promote and value minority languages. to appreciate the challenge of multilingualism, we must understand its substance. indeed, cultural and linguistic diversity leads to respect for cultural identity, traditions and religions. by encouraging the construction of a european society of 'plural' knowledge, europe implicitly recognises that language learning is a crucial factor in the ability of peoples to communicate with one another. multilingualism is also an opportunity for the future and safeguarding it has become a duty for europe's citizens. in the face of globalisation, which favours monolingualism, the more linguistic diversity is recognised, the less opportunities for identity withdrawal there will be.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, by adopting the council regulation of 27 june 2005 reforming the system of preferences in force since 1971, the european union chose to simplify and strengthen its main trade instrument for supporting developing countries. three schemes are now applicable: the general system, the everything but arms system, which is a tool adapted to the specific needs of the least developed countries, and finally the gsp+. the additional preferences granted under the latter strand arise from the conviction that development can only be envisaged in close connection with the process of democratisation and respect for human rights, labour law and the environment. fifteen countries are currently benefiting from this mechanism, which provides both incentives and rewards to developing countries that are the most vulnerable and make the most effort in these areas. but for gsp+ to really contribute to better governance and greater respect for the environment, human rights and labour, it must be managed effectively, which means firstly warning the many countries that still do not respect their commitments and, above all, moving from the enchanting threats to the effective removal of the preferences granted to those who seriously and systematically violate ilo conventions and do not honour their obligations. secondly, there is a need for regular assessment of the fulfilment of commitments by each gsp+ beneficiary country. it should be particularly comprehensive with a view to renewing this instrument at the end of 2008. our credibility and the effectiveness of this instrument depend on what the jurists call the parallelism of forms. we cannot continue to grant these preferences to countries which are politically incapable of meeting these commitments. the future of this policy is at stake.
