creation, promotion and strengthening of participatory and representative democracy, including parliamentary democracy, and the corresponding processes of democratization. i would also like to see the possible financing of foundations as a way of bridging our difficulties. the most important thing for us has been that we, as the commission, have been able to be neutral and impartial in community aid. we have a great advantage in this respect and we must maintain it in the future. this is the reason for the high acceptance and potential of our aid in third countries. so we should not deviate from that here either.
the committee mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since september my co-rapporteur and i have been negotiating with the council and the commission to put forward parliament's position on the european financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights in the world. the negotiations are now closed and, as has just been said, the council adopted a common position last week based on a compromise text. this text, which we have already largely tabled in the form of amendments, covers most of parliament's requests. it states that the use of this instrument does not require the agreement of the governments of third states. it allows funding for unregistered organisations. it includes a flexible mechanism for direct support to human rights defenders at risk. this new mechanism should make our work to protect those who work for freedoms much more effective. the compromise also contains a whole section on the promotion of democracy, democratic processes and parliamentary democracy. the political foundations and also the national parliaments, and this is an element introduced by our parliament, are explicitly mentioned among the eligible actors. the protection of human rights also covers almost all of parliament's requests, with the exception of explicit references to the fight against impunity and conflict prevention. on the other hand, the rights of disabled people, corporate social responsibility, the fight against violence against women and many others have been integrated. parliament also secured the establishment of a comprehensive dialogue mechanism which involves it in the development of strategic priorities. we would have liked to have had it in the text, but the compromise was to codify it by an exchange of letters. as regards an explicit reference to democratic political groups, the council, as has just been said, considers that this is a red line for it. it was therefore not possible to introduce explicit references to their support. however, flexibility has been introduced in the text to allow for the financing, in duly justified cases, of other actors. thus, in certain situations, support may be given to political groups without explicit mention. in conclusion, mr president, i should like to stress the uniqueness of this instrument. it is the only one to finance projects of non-state actors without requiring prior authorization from their government. it is also the only instrument financing election observation missions. the delay in adopting it, and therefore the funding of these projects in the vain hope of introducing an explicit reference to political groups, would therefore be neither useful nor responsible. the persistence in wanting to do so has already led us to lose the compromise reached with the council on the integration of the rights of migrants and asylum seekers. for these reasons, i would ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to confirm the compromise as negotiated with the council.
mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we should be proud to be members of the european union when we see its action in promoting democracy and human rights. these common values make the union a key player on the international scene in these matters. in this constant struggle, it was essential to reform the old instrument to make it more effective. it is thanks to the tenacity of the rapporteurs, mrs flautre and mr mcmillan-scott, whom i congratulate, that we have before us a text which shows real progress. it was an important instrument, and it had to be ambitious. this is particularly the case with references to the rights of migrants and the possibility of overriding the endorsement of third countries in order to promote democracy and human rights. i regret, however, that the negotiations have not led to the extension of the scope of this instrument to conflict prevention. in addition, despite the increased involvement of parliament in monitoring, the council's refusal to formalise relations between the two institutions on this subject is a defect. in conclusion, the effectiveness of this instrument will depend on its regular evaluation and review: parliament will have to play its full part in this, because i believe that this is a fight for a europe of values for a world without fear.

research, i believe we have agreed a very responsible ethical framework for a research programme covering so many different countries. it continues the ethical framework of framework programme 6, which has proved successful in practice. the commission has made an extensive declaration on this ethical framework, which will be published in the official journal as part of the framework programme 7 package. the commission will fully respect and strictly implement this declaration, which i consider to be an integral part of the agreement on framework programme 7. accordingly, the commission will not fund projects that include research activities which destroy human embryos, including for the procurement of stem cells. the exclusion of funding of this step of research will not prevent community funding of subsequent steps involving human embryonic stem cells. even if article 6(3) of the decision on framework programme 7 refers to derivation, the commission will not fund derivation that involves destroying a human embryo. the agreement on ethics reflects a careful and responsible balance. the commission calls on the european parliament not to jeopardise this balance by any further amendment. i now come to the seven specific programmes, which set out the details of the two framework programmes for research. to a large extent, the modifications of the commission’s proposals were concerned with transposing the provisions of the agreed framework programme into the specific programme texts. following these changes, the final draft presidency texts on the specific programmes include a welcome mixture of parliament’s requests and the council’s own reflections, making these texts perfectly compatible with the commission’s position. for the specific programme on cooperation, parliament’s amendments being put to the vote are, generally speaking, coherent with the framework programme text and largely acceptable. this is also thanks to the excellent work of the rapporteur, ms riera madurell. it was not an easy task to deal with such a broad range of fields with important research challenges. let me just mention as an example of our strong cooperation the agreement reached on renewables and energy efficiency. for the ideas programme, the european parliament’s main concerns, as reflected in the amendments and discussed intensively during the tripartite meetings, have been taken into account. due consideration has been given, in particular, to: the ceiling on the administrative costs of the total budget; questions related to the management staff of the european research council; a clearly defined approach to the process of selection, term of office and renewal of the members of the scientific council; the reference to the review of erc structures and mechanisms and the possibility of the scientific council appointing a secretary-general. once more, thanks to the rapporteur ms niebler and to mr ehler for their constructive work. for the people programme, the current presidency text has taken on board a number of parliament’s amendments, which are fully acceptable to the commission. i would highlight in particular those that refer to the importance of encouraging youngsters to enter the research profession, of helping them with a more stable career path, and making full use of women’s potential. i offer all my thanks for the support given by the rapporteur, mr pirilli. on the capacities specific programme, let me highlight some of those amendments that really improved the commission’s original proposal. i am referring, in particular, to those clarifying the role of rtd performers for activities under research for the benefit of smes and the introduction of mechanisms for cooperation with national and regional r&d support programmes. concerning research potential activities, the addition of the reference to the associated countries clarifies and emphasises the eligibility of entities from these countries to participate in the actions supported under this specific programme. the constant and useful support received from the rapporteur, mr prodi, has been really appreciated. on the ec joint research centre specific programme, i am glad to see that parliament supports the priorities of the jrc as indicated in the specific programme. i agree with the majority of the amendments tabled, which are aimed at better defining the jrc mission in relation to its different activities. in particular, i agree to the request regarding the role that the jrc could play in providing a sustainable energy reference system and information on the reliability of the energy supply for europe, as well as on the availability of renewable energy resources. thank you for your excellent work, mr hammerstein mintz. regarding the euratom specific programme, the text is broadly acceptable with some minor exceptions. thank you to the rapporteur, mr guidoni, for his strong support for the commission’s proposal. let me open a parenthesis here just to say that the iter project has been of paramount importance. i must say that i feel fortunate to have been directly involved. last week, i had the honour of taking part in the ceremony in paris and, as i said there, i am confident that ‘hard winds grow strong trees’. i also thought of you, mr busquin, at that moment. on the euratom joint research centre specific programme, i am pleased to see that the european parliament and the council support the commission’s approach and that the proposed amendments improve the commission proposal. and i share the request expressed by the parliament that "in view of the threat of a loss of knowledge and a lack of new scientists and engineers in the area of nuclear technology,[...] the jrc will implement a programme aimed at retaining knowledge, ensuring that this knowledge is readily available, properly organised and well documented." once more, thanks for the support received from the rapporteur, mr caspary. let me now turn to the reports by mr busquin and ms laperrouze on the ec and euratom rules for participation respectively. the commission is very grateful to the european parliament and, in particular, to the rapporteurs, shadow rapporteurs and other members of the itre committee for their constructive attitude and strong commitment to reaching a good compromise with the council, allowing the adoption of the ec framework programme 7 rules for participation at first reading. this follows the welcome precedent established under framework programme 6 and i am confident that this cooperation will continue in the future. the euratom rules will follow the same principles as those agreed for the ec rules, taking into account the necessary adjustments due to the specificities of the framework programme 7 euratom framework programme. concerning the busquin and laperrouze reports, the commission can accept all elements of the agreement reached between the european parliament and the council. there is no doubt that the final text provides for significant improvements to the original commission proposal. i would like to highlight the following elements of the agreement on the rules for participation. firstly, the coverage and calculation of indirect costs, in particular the flat rate introduced for non-profit public bodies, universities, research organisations and smes. this flat rate is now fixed at 60% for the first three years (2007-2009) and thereafter the commission shall establish a new flat rate reflecting an approximation of the real indirect costs of participants, but not lower than 40%. you have been very persuasive in convincing both the council and the commission in this respect. secondly, the participants’ guarantee fund, which replaces collective financial responsibility, as it was known under fp6. this fund will be established by the commission and will serve as a basis for exempting from verification participants – with the exception of project coordinators – requesting less than eur 500 000 for a project. moreover, no additional guarantee or security may be requested from participants or imposed on them, which will particularly help smes and other small users. thirdly, the evaluation criteria will be clearly established in the framework programme 7 rules. fourthly, there is the clarification regarding the financial statements, where the compromise agreed reflects parliament and the council’s common goal of simplifying and limiting the number of certificates. fifthly, the 75% upper funding limit for security-related research in the case of the development of highly reliable capabilities has an impact on the security of european citizens and is aimed at a limited number of public users. parliament’s wish has been fully satisfied in this respect. finally, there are the access rights for european affiliates established in a member state or associated country, which they will enjoy if they are required to use their own foreground under the same conditions as the participant to which they are affiliated. i reiterate my warmest thanks for your excellent work, mr busquin and mrs laperrouze. before concluding, i would like to come to a topic that concerns at least some of you, as indicated by the amendments tabled. this concerns the participation of entities established in territories that are not internationally recognised. i understand that the aim is to exclude legal entities operating in the territories occupied by israel. since august 1996, israel has been fully associated to the framework programme for research and development. israel’s research bodies are today valued and active partners in the implementation of the framework programme. the commission has therefore recommended that the council should renew the association agreement for the lifetime of framework programme 7. the association agreements in combination with the rules for participation give legal entities established in israel the same rights and obligations concerning participation and funding as a legal entity established in a member state. only legal entities which are established within the internationally recognised territory of israel can be considered as such legal entities under the text of the rules for participation before you. legal entities established in the occupied territories cannot be considered as israeli legal entities as defined by the fp6 rules for participation and the association agreement. the commission will be very vigilant in this regard. let me conclude by saying that i have really appreciated these 19 months of intense work and friendly collaboration. many amendments have a special meaning for me, as they remind me of each of you, from mr liese’s interest in children’s disease to ms riera madurell’s and ms gutiérrez-cortines’s strong support for cultural heritage; from mr prodi’s strong defence of the european technology platforms to mr hammerstein mintz’s and mr turmes’s attention to renewable energy sources, and mr busquin’s strong support for the guarantee fund, to mention just a few. i believe our cooperation bodes well for the implementation of the seventh framework programme and for the continued development of ambitious research and innovation policies that europe needs and deserves. the debate today and the vote tomorrow herald the start of a new journey, one that i hope will see europe cross frontiers and reach new horizons. researchers will know that the european institutions are there to support them on this journey. yes, this evening and tomorrow at midday are truly important hours for europe and european science. we can truly be proud of what we have achieved and of the direction of the scientific journey on which we have embarked together for a better life for all europeans and for the whole of humanity. the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, madam minister, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to commend the work done by my fellow rapporteurs and, more generally, by the three institutions to enable the 'research' package to be adopted swiftly. the seventh framework programme is the key tool for the realisation of the european research area with the objective of devoting 3% of gdp to research. it should increase synergies and complementarities between national policies and ensure greater coherence between the priorities of the member states and the broad lines to be defined by the european research council. despite a budget that is less substantial than the commission and parliament had hoped for, this framework programme must be appreciated for its leverage effect. to overcome the difficulties in accessing finance, especially for smes, the introduction of the financing and risk-sharing mechanism is a step in the right direction. the mechanism should make it possible to increase the number of loans granted by the european investment bank and financial institutions, to commit larger amounts and to support more risky projects. as regards the rules for the participation of the european atomic energy community in the seventh framework programme, my approach has been to work closely with mr busquin, rapporteur on the rules of the conventional rdp, in order to maintain the similarity of these two texts and thereby to take advantage of the codecision procedure. the compromise amendments which we are proposing to you are therefore the result of discussions between the commission, the council and parliament on mr busquin's report, and are adapted to the field of atomic energy. two amendments, however, differ from the council's position. we wanted to clarify the award criteria in amendment no 58, such as scientific excellence, the ability to carry out the action successfully, relevance to the objectives of the specific programme, the critical mass of resources, the quality of the plan for the exploitation and dissemination of the knowledge acquired. i would also draw your attention to amendment no 88 in this report, which some colleagues have asked for a separate vote. this amendment does not preclude the choice of barcelona as the seat of the joint undertaking. the location of the headquarters is clearly set out in council decision 2006/458 and we support it. the aim of this amendment is to ensure that the other activities planned under the fusion energy thematic area are implemented and managed separately from the joint undertaking, so that researchers can develop their creative potential. this separation would thus make it possible to maintain the integrated approach and the strong involvement of the fusion associations through, in particular, the european agreement for the development of fusion. during the trilogues with the commission and the council on the rules of participation, this issue was raised mr president, on 22 june 2006 the european commission presented a communication to respond to the crisis of overproduction in the european wine sector. the commission is recommending that 400 000 hectares of vineyards be grubbed up in the next five years, or almost 12% of the 3.4 million hectares in the european union. i would like to draw your attention today to the existence of illegal vine plantations in europe: they are estimated to cover an area of 150 000 hectares for the whole of the european union. according to the commission's own figures, in a report of march 2004, these illegal vine plantations would have produced between 5 and 8 million hectolitres, even though european overproduction is estimated at 12 million hectolitres. the permanent uprooting of these illegal vines would restore a form of balance. so before any decision is taken on grubbing-up measures, i ask the commission to draw up a precise picture of these illegal plantations.
president of the council. mr president, mr sacconi, members of the european parliament, mr verheugen and mr dimas, the reach regulation is one of the most important legislative projects in the history of the european union. the regulation will be a major leap forward from the current chemical control system, which is about 40 years old. it is a fact that europe is a global pioneer and a global leader. for almost three years, the european parliament, the council and the commission have worked together to adopt the reach regulation. the negotiation process has been a difficult one. i think it is no exaggeration to say that without the strong commitment of all parties to this issue, we would not be here today. in the council, the preparation of the regulation has been the challenge of seven presidencies. i would like to thank all the presidencies in the council who have prepared the ground for the decision now before us. the political agreement reached in the council during the uk presidency provided an excellent basis for the conclusion of the negotiations during the finnish presidency. i am very pleased that the member states have given their strong support to the negotiated compromise package. i also warmly hope that the various groups in the european parliament will support the compromise resolution as widely as possible in the vote on wednesday. i would like to thank the european parliament for its excellent cooperation during the autumn negotiations. i would like to thank in particular the rapporteur, mr saccon, and mr florenz, chairman of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, the shadow rapporteurs, and many other representatives who have worked actively to find common solutions. i would also like to thank commissioners verheugen and dimas for their strong personal contribution to the negotiations. at this stage in the process, it is a good time to assess how the objectives of reach as a whole are being achieved. the regulation will significantly improve the protection of human health and the environment. reach improves our knowledge of the properties of substances, enhances the management of chemical risks and requires authorisation for the most dangerous substances. the new security requirements will be the most demanding in the world. it is in the common interest of european consumers and industry to promote the development of new and safer chemicals. to this end, the current procedure for the notification of new substances has been reformed in the proposal. reach also increases the responsibilities and duties of companies and allows them to manage their chemical safety obligations more independently than before. the transparency of chemical control will be considerably increased by the creation of modern information systems and registers at the agency, which will also provide citizens with better information on substances and their properties. information systems will be unique in the world. the study of the effects of substances requires better knowledge of their properties. reach takes this area to a new level by allowing the widespread use of alternative research methods and programmes. these new alternative methods are likely to have an impact on chemical testing on a global scale. consumers are also getting more information about the dangerous substances contained in goods. reach also establishes a system whereby traders are obliged to provide information on substances of very high concern contained in articles, upon request by the consumer. the question of the authorisation procedure and substitutions was the last open point in the negotiations. in accordance with the proposal of the presidency, the applicant or the authorisation holder should submit a substitution plan when an analysis of the alternatives indicates that suitable alternatives exist. the substitution plan must be submitted irrespective of whether the authorisation is granted on the basis of appropriate risk management or socioeconomic benefits. in addition, the appropriate risk management pathway was narrowed compared to the common position so that it does not apply to pbt and vpvb substances. for endocrine disruptors, a review was agreed within six years. i believe that this solution takes account in a balanced and realistic way of the concerns expressed by the european parliament about the substitution of the most dangerous substances. as president-in-office of the council, i am pleased to announce that a package of amendments based on the results of the trialogue negotiations is to be voted on. i can confirm the council's approval of these amendments. as regards the other amendments, i hope that the outcome of the negotiations will remain unchanged. i hope that parliament will adopt the compromise package negotiated with the council on the regulation at its meeting on wednesday. this would bring a major legislative project of importance to european citizens and industry one step closer to reality. member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, these days a long legislative process is coming to an end and reach is taking its final form. the commission, as vice-president verheugen said, congratulates the council and parliament on reaching an agreement. the agreement aims to improve health and environmental protection and to promote innovation and industrial competitiveness. the commission therefore supports the package of compromise proposals agreed between the council and parliament on 30 november 2006. i would like to thank the presidency and the minister, mr pekkarinen, and of course the european parliament, the committee on the environment, its chairman, mr florenz, and especially the rapporteur, mr guido sacconi, for the considerable efforts and determination which have brought this proposal to a successful conclusion. reach is one of the most comprehensive, ambitious and far-reaching pieces of legislation that has been drawn up in the european union to date. it will affect all sectors of industry, but also ordinary citizens in direct or more indirect ways, as chemicals are so widespread in our daily lives. for citizens and consumers, reach means better information on substances in everyday products, but above all it means that the most dangerous substances will be gradually replaced by safer ones. the commission also stressed that risk assessments would take special account of vulnerable groups such as children, pregnant women and the elderly. this will also improve the health of citizens and prevent environmental damage, which is not only costly to treat and manage but often irreversible. for industry, reach means a general responsibility to avoid adverse effects on health and the environment from the production, use and sale of chemicals. it also means that the flow of information in the production chain will be improved so that downstream users have a better and more complete knowledge of the characteristics and properties of the substances they use. this will make it possible to set more precise targets for risk management measures, which will enhance the protection of workers and thus reduce health and occupational problems. although there will be some cost increase, this expenditure and investment will be spread over a long period of time, e.g. 11 years in the case of registration or even more years in the case of lending. the new system is expected to restore consumer confidence in chemicals and the chemical industry and, moreover, reach will boost competitiveness and innovation, which will not only offset but also exceed most of the initial costs and investments. reach aims to reduce animal testing to the absolute minimum. the agreement between parliament and the council on this point is satisfactory. it stresses the importance of alternative methods and provides for a 45-day public consultation period for each test proposal. the vote on wednesday will be the final stage in a process aimed at achieving the target set by the heads of state or government at the 2006 spring meeting of completing reach by the end of 2006. i hope, therefore, that we can complete the process as planned, that the regulation comes into force and that we can begin to tackle the great challenge that lies ahead of us, namely to gradually gather knowledge about the thousands of substances in use today and to put in place improved risk management measures. finally, ladies and gentlemen, we must begin, and we must begin soon, with the gradual substitution of dangerous substances. if there are alternative products available, substitution should be our first choice.

vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament has been a great help to us. i would like to make just two brief remarks. some of the participants in the debate, whom i do not see at the moment, criticised the fact that the reach project would reduce the level of protection for workers in the chemical industry. i must say with all firmness that this is simply nonsense. reach cannot reduce the level of protection in the chemical industry. the relevant occupational safety and health provisions remain fully in force. reach does not allow anything that was previously prohibited. on the contrary, a whole series of substances which workers have been exposed to will no longer be attributed to them. so reach is definitely making a significant improvement in the safety of workers at work. i therefore have to reject this argument very clearly from members of this house who pretend to represent the interests of workers. the second point i would like to make is that many speakers have rightly pointed out that what is needed now is to implement reach in a non-bureaucratic, transparent, decisive and full way. this requires an infinite number of initiatives, projects and measures. i could tell you all about them, but i don't have time. i have already offered the chairman of the environment committee to come to the committee in february and report in detail on the measures that the commission has either already taken or is planning to take with regard to the implementation of reach. i would like to stress the importance of answering all the questions that have been raised here, which relate to facilitating and helping the small and mediumsized enterprises in europe and the many hundreds of thousands of workers affected by them.

member of the commission. mr president, first of all i would like to thank the committee on the internal market and consumer protection as well as the other committees involved, and in particular mrs fourtou as rapporteur for the reports to be discussed tonight. the modernisation of the european customs environment is an essential contribution to attaining the objectives of the lisbon strategy. it is a must if we want the european union to remain an attractive place to do business and maintain the external competitiveness of eu companies. in this context, it is crucial to deepen the single market by making the eu a fully-integrated customs territory. this reform is also critical if we want to live up to the challenges of globalisation and reinforce the role of customs in protecting our citizens and companies from security and safety hazards such as counterfeiting, dangerous goods or the devices of international terrorism. the modernised community customs code will provide the legal framework for the development of a simple and paperless environment for customs and trade based on the best use of information and communication technology. the present community customs code was adapted in 1992. since then, it has undergone only limited changes. this means that the code has not kept pace with the radical changes to the environment in which customs and traders operate, particularly in respect of the rapid and irreversible adoption of electronic data exchange. the customs code has to be adapted to fit the electronic environment. in addition, it is commonly held by customs authorities and traders alike that current customs procedure and processes are unnecessarily complicated. they also do not reflect the changing focus of customs work, moving from the collection of declining customs duties towards the application of non-tariff measures. this includes, in particular, security and safety measures, the fight against counterfeiting, money laundering and drugs and the application of sanitary, health and consumer protection measures. with your support, the proposal for a modernised customs code on the table tonight, together with the proposals on the council table and e-customs, will make customs work better, faster and more cheaply. let me once again and now more specifically turn to mrs fourtou and the committee on the internal market for their detailed and most valuable assessment of the commission’s proposal for a modernised customs code. i know there is unanimous support in the committee on the internal market for the rapporteur’s recommendations. progress in the council is complementing your work. i am pleased to report that on 4 december the competitiveness council showed a keen interest in the key elements of the reform. ministers gave strong support to the commission’s proposals on the single window, on centralised clearance and on customs agents, while inviting the commission to pursue the work to implement these in an acceptable manner for all member states. i would like to thank parliament for its constructive contribution to the debate on these three issues, but i must also inform you that in at least one of them the commission’s position remains unchanged. thus it is the commission’s firm opinion that the accreditation of professional customs agents is not a matter for the customs code. there is a future for the profession in an open competitive market, through self-regulation and the recognition provided by the status of authorised economic operator. though there is no debate on the e-customs proposal tonight, i would like to take this opportunity to thank the rapporteur mr heaton-harris and the committee on the internal market for its full support for an extremely ambitious commission proposal. it is indeed challenging to propose that all member states and the commission commit themselves to developing common electronic systems for customs proposals by an agreed date. let me stress that the firm support from parliament is more than welcome in order to convince member states that, despite budgetary constraints, they need to develop their customs it system in a community framework. i am confident that the council will acknowledge this step and the proposal can soon be adopted. i very much appreciate the efforts of the european parliament and particularly those of mrs fourtou to come to an agreement in a single reading on the customs 2013 proposal. this will definitely ensure the continuity of the programme activities as of 1 january 2008. the speedy adoption of customs 2013 shows that there is a broad agreement across all the institutions on the obvious need to guarantee the effective functioning of the internal market in the customs field. indeed, the customs environment is undergoing major changes. the customs 2013 programme will be an essential instrument to ensure efficient cooperation and coordination between all customs administrations. it will facilitate the introduction of new trans-european computerised systems, reinforce networks between customs officials and promote and establish common training modules. once the two customs proposals under debate and the e-customs proposal are finally adopted by both parliament and the council, they will enable the customs services of the eu to meet the major challenges. they will facilitate international trade, foster simpler control and will more effectively protect the internal market and the health, safety and security of our citizens through more efficient control.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the three reports on the customs code, modernised, customs without paper, customs programme 2013 which are being discussed at this part-session show the growing importance of customs and their role in the european union's desire for competitiveness and efficiency. these three reports are closely linked, but for the sake of clarity i will first present the modernised customs code and then move on to the customs 2013 programme. the customs code - you said it, mr kovacs - dates from 1992. it was legitimate to modernise it to adapt it to the evolution of customs duties and the radical changes in international trade. the aim is to streamline customs procedures by laying the foundations for accessible and interoperable customs clearance systems throughout the european union. that is why this proposal is accompanied by a proposal for a decision on electronic customs, for which my colleague, mr heaton-harris, is the rapporteur. the new code has 200 articles, in which we have concentrated on the main points, or at least on the most controversial points, namely the customs representative, the authorized economic operator, centralised customs clearance and comitology. article 11 deals with the customs representative. until now, national legislation could reserve the right of representation to a professional category. however, in the context of the single market and the electronic environment, this monopoly no longer has any place. in addition, some companies may have an integrated service that handles customs formalities. the right to customs representation should therefore be open to all. however, in many member states the use of customs agents is traditional and remains very useful for small businesses. the commission has therefore adopted an amendment which, without wishing to maintain a monopoly, provides that, as one of the criteria for the status of customs representative, account should be taken of the existence of practical standards of competence or professional qualifications in order to satisfy member states for whom the abolition of this monopoly is difficult to accept. we have not yet found the ideal solution and this question will certainly be raised again at second reading because some delegations in the council still express reservations and even go so far as to ask for regulated access to the profession. the authorised economic operator is a new feature introduced into the customs code by regulation 648 of 13 april 2005, known as the 'security regulation'. this status has not yet become a reality in itself, since the implementing provisions have just been adopted by the commission. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has introduced a clarification, making a clear distinction between authorized economic operator - customs simplification, and authorized economic operator - security. the centralised clearance is a welcome facilitation in principle but member states have questions about the collection of customs duties. the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has taken a rather radical position by calling for free electronic customs clearance and the possibility of opening customs offices 24 hours a day. in order to ensure fair competition between national customs authorities, the rule must be common to all. however, it will be necessary to ensure that there is harmonisation of control activities. finally, the provisions of the proposal refer constantly to comitology. this procedure is necessary because experts are needed to draw up the implementing provisions of the code. under the new interinstitutional agreement of july 2006, certain provisions of the code are subject to the new comitology procedure with scrutiny. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a breach of the directive is a very good one. the committee on international trade adopted amendments in favour of the codecision procedure for certain provisions which would normally fall within its competence under the enhanced cooperation procedure. however, we considered that his position was contrary to that of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and we had to reject those amendments. so that is very briefly the main points of the dossier and, as i said earlier, it is also closely linked to the dossier relating to the customs 2013 programme. the mid-term evaluation of the customs 2007 programme has shown that it is well-suited to the needs of administrations and plays a key role in helping participating countries to share their experiences. the evaluation recommended strengthening activities in the areas of training and dissemination of information. the programme has a budget of eur 322.8 million over six years and aims to help the customs administrations of the participating countries to promote legitimate trade, simplify and speed up customs procedures and ensure the safety and protection of the citizens and financial interests of the community. the amendments adopted by the committee on the internal market and consumer protection are in line with the council's work and i am particularly grateful to the finnish presidency for having negotiated with the member states on several occasions to meet the legitimate budgetary demands of the european parliament and defended our position. i hope that this will enable us to conclude this dossier at the first reading. customs files are highly technical and complex. i would therefore like to thank my various contacts in the taxation dg who have always answered all my requests and made it easier for me to address these issues. i also thank my colleagues and the chairman of our committee for their help and support. at a time when trade is accelerating, when organised crime and counterfeiting threaten our security and our market, customs and economic operators need all our support.

the rapporteur. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european union is therefore preparing today to reform the internal part of the cmo in the banana sector, in order to adapt the aid scheme for european producers to the new world trade situation and to the principles of the new common agricultural policy. this amendment, which is the subject of the report submitted to the house today after being approved by a very large majority in parliament's committee on agriculture, is undoubtedly going in the right direction. for banana producers in the outermost regions, who account for more than 98% of eu production, it is planned to transfer an amount of almost €280 million per year to the posei programmes, which will bring greater flexibility and therefore better use of community funds. i would like to thank you, commissioner, for the reassessment of the sums allocated to this reform, which should make it possible to ensure the sustainability of the sector, particularly in the outermost regions where bananas play a fundamental economic and social role that no other agricultural production can compensate for. i should like to remind you, however, that the amounts proposed were calculated on the basis of the current customs tariff. however, uncertainty surrounding global trade negotiations suggests that this tariff level will fall further. the banana sector, at 176 euros per tonne, is already in a situation of extreme fragility which threatens the socioeconomic balance of many producing regions. a further reduction in the customs tariff would be the death knell for community banana production if no adjustments were made to the plan proposed by the commission. if the opening up of markets can help to boost production structures, it can only do so if the fundamental principles of regulation and fairness are met, namely the respect by the various producers of common rules which place them on an equal commercial footing, an equality which is clearly totally absent from world trade today, given the gap between the social and environmental standards of european countries and those of central and latin american countries. in view of this problem, the solution of which must remain a priority for the european union, aid to community banana producers is a necessity to compensate for the malfunctions of the world trade system. to be effective, these internal control measures must be in line with external control tools. it is with this in mind that the committee on agriculture insists on strengthening the evaluation measures provided for in the reform proposal, so that the commission can take concrete measures if the external tariff situation were to deteriorate, for example by increasing the amount of financial envelopes allocated to producers. the sustainability of the european banana sector also depends on its ability to optimise its production costs while respecting social rules and farmers' living standards. since the creation of the cmo, producer organisations have thus helped to achieve a better concentration of supply of community bananas on the market and have contributed to a significant reduction in the burden of banana cultivation in the union. it would be economically contradictory to break this dynamic today. we therefore consider it essential to maintain a relevant regulatory framework at community level for producer organisations in order to continue the efforts made to strengthen our production structures. as requested by the committee on agriculture, this will also have to be reflected in the obligation to be a member of a producer organisation in order to be eligible for the aid otherwise provided for under the posei envelope, except where circumstances do not allow it. finally, and this is my last point, there is the question of the management of aid. the system of production support under the current banana cmo provides for two-monthly advance payments which are essential for the sector's activities in the outermost regions as well as in the rest of the union's producing countries. the transfer of the funds to the posei programmes is not accompanied by a renewal of this system of advances, endangering the survival of the producers who would then be forced to borrow privately, even though the uncertainty characterising the business environment in this sector does not encourage banks to grant long-term loans. in this context of economic instability, it is up to the european public authorities to provide sufficient guarantees to ensure that the situation generated by these trade policy choices at world level does not run counter to the interests of the union's most vulnerable farmers.
bananas are a structural element of the economy of 4 of the 7 ors, due to the importance of european outlets and the exceptional need for labour it requires. our parliament must ensure that the proposed support is set at a sufficient level and takes account of possible changes in the tariff in the context of the wto negotiations. to deal with any deterioration in the incomes of producers, it is necessary to provide for an automatic revision clause and to re-establish the current system of financial advances, which are essential for the activity of the sector. overseas banana producers are waiting for a clear signal about the sustainability of the sector, to restore confidence in it. the caribbean banana sector, which has long been fragmented and inefficient, is now a model of organization whose efforts to restructure must be emphasized. i would remind you that the banana sector in the ors complies with the non-commercial criteria in force in the union, unlike its competitors in latin american countries. without the banana, which provides 15 000 jobs and is the economic backbone of these regions in terms of human, social and environmental needs, the whole of guadeloupe and martinique's agriculture would be threatened with extinction, in the absence of alternative production.

member of the commission. mr president, i would like to thank parliament and in particular the rapporteur, mrs bachelot, for her tireless efforts to make progress in the negotiations on the european globalisation adjustment fund. i would also like to take this opportunity to thank the finnish presidency for its efforts to ensure that the egf proposal is adopted at first reading. the fact that the fund will be adopted at first reading is a clear political signal. it shows that the european union cares about its citizens. we should not forget why this fund is created. no one disputes the benefits of global trade to our labour markets and our economies. in some areas, however, the opening up of world trade has caused changes in the structure of our economies, and this has resulted in significant job losses. many times we can anticipate change, we can respond at a given stage with existing support mechanisms such as the european social fund, but sometimes it is simply impossible to predict where and when job losses will occur and how much impact they will have, and now the egf will help us to respond to such crises. from the outset, the commission has highlighted the importance of this fund for european citizens. this fund is a very concrete expression of european solidarity. for example, in recent years the egf has been able to play a role in compensating for the significant job losses that have occurred as a result of changes in the textile industry. when the textile and clothing quotas were abolished under the wto agreement on textiles and clothing at the end of 2004, many workers in the sector in europe were at risk of redundancy. the regions affected included valencia and catalonia in spain and the south-west region of the czech republic. similarly, in recent years there have been significant redundancies in the footwear industry, for example in the french region of pas de la loire, also in the hungarian region of western danube. this is where the egf could help workers find new jobs, acquire new skills and qualifications or take the big step of starting their own business. the commission proposal was based on the council's mandate to set up a fund specifically designed to provide additional support for workers who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes in the nature of world trade. the criteria for aid proposed by the commission reflect the council's request that assistance from the fund be subject to clear criteria depending on the extent of the disturbance and its impact on local, regional and national economies. in the current version of the text adopted, the positions of parliament and the council are optimally balanced. both the council and the parliament supported the criteria for granting aid, which apply to large companies on the one hand and to smes on the other. the flexibility clause, which should take account of the concerns of member states with smaller labour markets as well as exceptional cases, has also received strong support. the regulation also provides member states with the opportunity to support a wide range of measures with the fund, depending on the nature of the crisis and the specific situation in each member state. i would like to thank you again, and especially mrs bachelot, for your efforts to get the fund set up and running from the beginning of 2007. now we must work together to ensure that all our instruments and policies benefit europeans. i am convinced that the combination of policies and efforts at national and eu level with the european social fund and now also the globalisation adjustment fund will bring real improvements for our people.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow we will be voting for the third time on the globalisation adjustment fund. the founding act of the project was the adoption of the böge report on the financial perspective 2007-2013. article 28 of the interinstitutional agreement thus defines, in addition to the draft fund, the annual amount of 500 million, budgeted over seven years, as well as part of the budgetary procedure. the second validation was expressed in the framework of the own-initiative report by jean louis cottigny on restructuring and employment, adopted last march: the latest events in the automobile sector tend to reinforce our vigilance on the future of economic sectors that are weak or in decline. i would like to take this opportunity to express my thoughts and solidarity with the workers affected by the accident at volkswagen in forest. parliament therefore expressed its support on two occasions for the conclusions of the hampton court summit, which endorsed the draft fund conceived by commission president josé manuel barroso. the committee on employment and social affairs adopted the report on the draft regulation on thursday, 26 october, by a very large majority, and this serves as the basis for the trilogue negotiations to obtain an agreement at first reading, so that, as you said, commissioner, the fund can be operational as from 1 january. the trilogue negotiations were concluded successfully on thursday, 30 november, with my agreement and that of president andersson and president lewandowski and the rapporteur for the opinion, esko seppänen, on the budgetary part, where he had enhanced cooperation. i would like to thank the fictitious rapporteurs for their constructive spirit - this is your report, mr jean louis cottigny, mr jean marie beaupuy and mrs elisabeth schroedter - and the group coordinators. i would also like to thank the representatives of the commission and the finnish presidency. the day after the trilogue, the agreement was ratified in the council by coreper: the agreement at first reading for the creation of the egf is therefore in the hands of the european parliamentarians, who will vote tomorrow. four principles have guided the work of our committee on employment and social affairs and we have preserved them throughout the debate. the first principle is european added value. it is not a question of substituting ourselves for the member states in the social treatment of industrial accidents. the egf will focus its assistance on emblematic cases of social disasters of european dimension following a change in the structure of international trade. the european parliament has therefore insisted in particular that the 50% co-financing rule be introduced in article 10 of our rules of procedure, thus marking european ambition and not the provision of european aid to national dossiers. we have also introduced the transnational element in certain cases. the second principle is responsibility. the european union, which is responsible for international trade negotiations, thus bears the potential consequences of its strategic choices. our responsibility is to take on board the positive aspects of globalisation, but also to take into account its potentially negative effects. third principle is justice. justice first, because we are addressing men and women. we have also rejected discrimination against small labour markets, which will now be eligible through the safeguard clause and the extension of the provisions of article 2 (b). the fourth principle is efficiency. in article 3 on eligible actions, we have clearly prohibited passive social protection measures. we want active measures to reintegrate workers, especially older workers, who must not be condemned to forced early retirement or prolonged unemployment. the egf programme thus finds its place in the lisbon strategy, as it will contribute to european competitiveness. efficiency also means monitoring and evaluating the process, which our parliament has placed a great deal of emphasis on. our aim is indeed to provide europe, through the egf, with an instrument similar to that which has already existed for 40 years in the united states with the trade adjustment act, which last year helped more than 170 000 american workers, of whom more than 75% have returned to longterm employment. many of my colleagues support the idea of the fund, but regret the lack of money. i understand them. i would like to stress, however, that this is an experimental approach which will have to be analysed, refined and supplemented. this experimental approach will be the first step towards establishing a genuine overall strategy for europe in globalisation. this strategy does not exist today and we cannot remain for long the only strategic trading player in the world without such a road map.

mr president, i would first like to thank mr stubb for his work on this very sensitive subject. the report has the merit of addressing the problem of the capacity for integration from different angles. i am therefore pleased that the text does not simply address the institutional aspects of this issue but also emphasises other major reforms, without which the union would not be able to welcome new members. i am thinking in particular of the revision of the union's financing system. i am also grateful to the rapporteur for having succeeded in ensuring the neutrality of this report vis-à-vis the applicant countries and avoiding the pitfall of expressing a position on the entry of one or another country. finally, this report rightly stresses the increased role that parliament should be given, not only in the context of the accession processes but also in the context of future institutional reforms. i would, however, like to make one criticism: it seems to me that the rapporteur, perhaps wanting to do too much, has somewhat diverted the report from its original purpose by making it more a report on the whole of the necessary reforms within the european union than on the more specific question of the capacity for integration. it would have been better, in my view, rather than listing a long list of institutional reforms, to concentrate on the only reforms which are the real prerequisites for any further enlargement.

mr president, allow me to make a point of order: there are - inevitably - many small difficulties in this text, many slight contradictions between the language versions. we did not want to raise these difficulties - i agree with what ruth hieronymi has just said. we think that in such an important debate, we should vote with the utmost simplicity. i would, however, like to see these linguistic contradictions removed when the text is passed from the commission to the council. that is why, mr president, i would like to see their existence mentioned in our minutes and that they are taken into account, because every word counts in a matter of such importance.
the rapporteur. mr president, thank you for giving me the floor. i would naturally like to thank mr lewandowski for withdrawing the amendments from the committee on budgets, which will make our task considerably easier. we are on the verge of an agreement at first reading and it will be a triple victory: a victory for european workers, a victory for the smooth functioning of our institutions and, i believe, a victory for ourselves, because we will have overcome our political and national divisions.
in writing. with today's vote, the eu has a text that is far from achieving the desired objectives. the project was ambitious: to adopt legislation allowing the registration and evaluation of chemicals with an obligation to substitute dangerous products when a less harmful alternative exists. this project did not withstand pressure from certain chemical industry lobbies, strongly echoed in the european parliament, which preferred to assert economic constraints at the expense of environmental protection and public health in order to obtain less restrictive legislation, in particular on substitution. i also regret that endocrine disruptors are excluded from the substitution procedure and that the chemical safety report is not mandatory for substances produced between one and ten tonnes. the agreement reached was insufficient, but rejecting it would have been to risk opening the conciliation procedure and ultimately producing a text that was completely devoid of meaning. this legislation, although insufficient, does exist and it is only on this merit that we are now mobilizing to demand financial and human resources to implement this regulation, to make progress and to ensure very gradual substitution.
in writing. the text put to the vote today brings to an end seven long years of hard work and debate between the chemical industry, which has been overusing the arguments of competitiveness and employment to defend the status quo, which is in its own financial interests, and european officials, who are keen to achieve responsible regulation to protect citizens from the dangers of dangerous chemicals in consumer products. of course, as is often the case, the result is not entirely in line with our expectations. as a result, the number of products covered by the reach regulation is only 30 000 compared to the 100 000 that were intended. but the progress is remarkable, especially when we consider that only 3 000 substances are currently being studied, or that it will now be the chemical industry that will bear the burden of proof of the toxicity of products, that is to say, that they are not harmful to humans. in the end, thanks to the tenacity of the socialist rapporteur, guido sacconi, the european union will have the most stringent legislation in the world on this subject. that is why i wholeheartedly supported the adoption of this text at second reading.
in writing. this agreement on reach will provide better protection for health and the environment and our european industry will have to be more responsible while remaining competitive on the global market. the text adopted contains a number of important improvements: reduction of bureaucracy, reduction of unnecessary testing, better protection of confidential information from companies and introduction of a compulsory substitution plan. the regulation will clarify legislation: the chemical sector is currently subject to some 40 european directives. the regulation will allow the registration of more than 30 000 chemical substances by the european chemicals agency over the next 11 years. i regret, however, that a lasting solution to the problem of imports from third countries has not been found. european importers of chemicals must register them, a procedure subject to reach. the problem is the import of finished products, the substances of which will simply be notified.
in writing. it is very important that the european union has a harmonised system for the registration, authorisation and control of chemical substances. an isolated member state cannot establish an effective system. this system must reduce the risks to our health and the environment and encourage innovation and support for economic activities that do not pollute. the compromise adopted today is a good response to the challenge of ambitious legislation which aims above all to create an effective system of protection for the individual, without hindering economic development.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise reached with the council on reach on 30 november, along with the three main political groups (epp-ed, pse and alde), so that our citizens can have legislation on the use of chemicals in our everyday products in place quickly - it is due to come into force on 1 april 2007. this is certainly a less ambitious compromise than the one i was seeking when i took the position at first reading that chemicals of 'extreme concern' should be replaced by compulsory substitution where safer alternatives exist. nevertheless, this compromise, the result of three years of preparation and difficult negotiations, is a delicate but necessary balance between the need to protect health and the environment and the competitiveness of enterprises. i hope, however, that the framework provided by reach will still allow substitution to gain real recognition, even if in practice a large number of toxic substances will escape it. it is the monitoring and control of the implementation of these regulations that will contribute to the consolidation of a stronger reach.
in writing. at first reading, we voted against the reach regulation on chemicals, considering that the amendments adopted did not allow us to achieve the balance announced between the three objectives of this regulation: protection of health and the environment, competitiveness and innovation and substitution of dangerous substances by alternative products that are less harmful or harmless. the compromise proposed today is not much more balanced. it is true that it has made considerable progress, as many speakers have pointed out in the debate: simplification of registration, increased practicability, some progress - insufficient - for smes, for example. but it also has its shortcomings and ambiguities, particularly as regards the constraints on imports and the disadvantages which may result for european manufacturers; it also concerns the application of the principle of substitution for dangerous substances alone, which is already a step forward, but without ensuring its effectiveness even if technically and economically viable alternatives exist. changing one imbalance for another is not the answer. none of the three initial aims of the directive will be achieved, nor will the simplification of legislation or its compatibility with other community legislation.
in writing. the fund is a new tool: for the first time, the eu will no longer only help companies or local authorities, but directly employees who have lost their jobs because of relocation. the european parliament has wanted to extend the benefit of this fund to the 'small labour markets' if redundancies have a serious impact on employment and the local economy. this opens up promising prospects for the most vulnerable areas in my region and i am delighted about this. i am also pleased with the unwavering commitment of the european socialists, who have strongly and tenaciously defended the introduction of this tool and have proposed many amendments to extend its implementation, amount and number of beneficiaries. it is a first step towards a more social and more united europe. the eu cannot, however, simply "cure the wounds" of globalisation. today, citizens expect europe to contribute to the security of their jobs and their way of life, just as it has been able to guarantee peace and stability for almost 50 years.
in writing. meps from the movement for france in the european parliament have refused to support the compromise proposed for the second reading vote on the draft directive on dangerous substances, known as reach. after its examination by the various european institutions, little remains of the original good intentions. the compromise text voted this morning is thus very inadequate in terms of environmental and consumer protection. furthermore, the new burdens it imposes on european companies are not offset by similar obligations imposed on imports of finished products, creating a distortion of competition which puts european industry at risk.
in writing. closely linked to the ambition of building a european union that brings people closer together, intercultural dialogue is now an important dimension of many community policies and instruments. i therefore welcome the adoption at second reading of the decision establishing the 2008 european year of intercultural dialogue. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs and security at first reading, i hope that this european year will enable all citizens, especially young people, to become aware of the need for intercultural dialogue in their everyday lives. it should highlight best practice in this area, in particular with regard to the integration of immigrants, in continuity with the actions undertaken in 2007 during the european year of equal opportunities for all. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. i am not sure how to describe ms bachelot-narquin's report on the european globalisation adjustment fund. yes, because under a tempting headline that makes it seem that brussels will help the economic and social victims of unbridled globalisation, there is a more down-to-earth reality: the criteria and modalities for allocating this fund give rise to fears that it will not go to the employees or the employment pools that need it. they can even encourage companies to adopt circumvention strategies or to look for bargaining chips. i am sure that the european social fund will be of help. the commission is pretending to help to mitigate the consequences of its own globalist economic and trade policies. it would be cheaper for the commission to challenge them for the benefit of european businesses and workers. but not useless for everyone, and especially very useful for brussels propaganda. article 9 of the regulation, which was reinforced by mrs bachelot's amendment no 38, provides that the member states must make it widely known that it is the commission which pays. as if this money did not come from the budget of the states, that is to say, from the pockets of the europeans themselves!
in writing. this european fund, with a maximum of eur 500 million per year, is intended to cushion the shocks of globalisation for workers affected by restructuring. this is not new aid to the firm but supplementary aid to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of changes in world trade. it will be granted under three conditions: at least 1 000 redundancies, with a serious impact on employment and the local economy and linked to a disruption in world trade. it can therefore only be used in the event of 'major changes in the structure of world trade leading to serious economic disruption', such as a massive increase in imports, a gradual decline in the eu market share in a sector, or a shift to third countries. i welcome the adoption of the globalisation adjustment fund, which will address citizens' concerns about the negative effects of globalisation and contribute to greater economic and social cohesion within the european union.
in writing. unlike the rapporteur, i do not believe that globalisation is a good thing for france and europe. the financial benefits of multinationals are one thing, the economic and social benefits in terms of employment and the defence of the european industrial fabric are another. the creation of a european globalisation adjustment fund, under the guise of trying to remedy relocations, will be just another bureaucratic and demagogic tool. if the europeans wanted to be more efficient and logical with themselves, they should have thought of improving and strengthening the european social fund. i believe that only the application of national and community preference and protection could save our jobs by redefining fair rules of world trade. the adjustment fund is also unacceptable, in particular because it seeks to challenge the action of the states, considering that solidarity efforts should be carried out only at the level of the european union and no longer at national or regional level. economic painkillers of this kind will not alleviate the social suffering of our peoples. the day of reckoning is approaching.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise on the creation of a european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). globalisation is a reality that can be beneficial when it is just and equitable. however, when globalisation has negative effects on workers, the european union must, in the interests of solidarity, correct the consequences of changes in the structure of world trade. the fund, which amounts to eur 500 million, will not be used to finance the restructuring of companies but to help workers made redundant, particularly in their reintegration into the labour market. the egf is an important instrument because it shows that the european union is fully aware of the social impact of globalisation and is not indifferent to the fate of workers. it was in 2005, seeing the impact of liberalisation and competition on the textile and clothing sector, and more particularly on its employees, that the idea of such a fund was born. it was only in 2007, two years later, that this fund became effective and responded in a concrete way to the expectations of the workers made redundant. yes, europe can be close to its citizens, and today it is proving it!
in writing. globalisation has negative consequences for the most vulnerable and least skilled workers in some sectors. the relocation of workers creates a climate of social insecurity which is detrimental to social progress. companies are taking advantage of a new freedom that ignores frontiers, leaving behind a cohort of employees, often with little training, who will have the greatest difficulty in finding work. 11 000 jobs have been relocated in the last 12 months in france. the fear of relocation is spreading from region to region, with nearly 1 000 jobs being lost every month, a figure which is more than enough to fuel social unrest. i voted in favour of mrs bachelot's report because it provides a first response to the legitimate concerns of european workers. the creation of a european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) will provide €500 million in annual support to workers affected by international restructuring to help them reintegrate into the labour market. the assistance provided by the egf should thus provide solidarity and support for workers made redundant as a result of changes in the structure of world trade, even if this fund is likely to prove insufficient.
in writing. transport is responsible for a large part of environmental pollution and has a major impact on climate change. the new euro 5 standard will focus on particulate matter and nitrogen oxides (nox) emitted by diesel vehicles. this further tightening of vehicle emission limits for particulate matter and nox is a significant step forward in terms of public health. the adoption of this report will strengthen the european union's commercial potential in the field of clean vehicle design and construction. the future euro 6 standard will contain restricted emission limits, in particular for nitrogen oxides, and at the same time stimulate technological research for the automotive industry. the text adopted also proposes a demanding but feasible implementation timetable for these two standards in the automotive sector. i believe, however, that we must continue to pay attention to the renewal of the car fleet and thus implement the latest euro standards if we are to hope for significant results on air quality.
mr president, bananas have been the subject of a real soap opera since the 1990s. in europe we consume bananas from three regions: european bananas from the french west indies, the canary islands and the azores, some 850 000 tonnes; bananas from the acp countries and, finally, dollar bananas grown in latin america for chiquita and dole. ten years ago, the customs duty on the 2.5 million tonnes of american bananas was almost 850 euros per tonne. today, they are 176 euros. in other words, europe is giving a gift of 2 billion euros to american multinationals. and these bananas are grown in ecuador by ten-year-olds who are paid $2 a day, who inhale pesticides, who have asthma, who have balance problems, who suffer from cerebral ataxia. elsewhere, similar conditions exist for those who work in greenhouses where roses are grown. under these circumstances, a carton of 18 kilos of bananas can be sold for 3 dollars in germany. it's called slavery. but it is true that our parliament also uses a form of slavery when it employs the auxiliary members of the assembly. my god, we're not even close to a slave!
in writing. no, the adoption of a constitution, the creation of a centralized european superstate are by no means an indispensable prerequisite for the enlargement of the european union. we will therefore, of course, vote against mr stubb's report, which attempts to bring in through the window this constitution which two european peoples have let out through the door. we must also ask ourselves, beyond these so-called 'institutional' aspects, which are more ideological in nature, whether it is not time to take a break. the european union has grown from 15 to 27 members in a very short time, and soon to 28. no one in this house is able to say today, beyond the agreed speeches, what the costs and benefits of this unprecedented enlargement are, either for the eu or for each of our states. enlargement for the sake of enlargement has no meaning except, as we object, the absorption of the nation states by the brussels leviathan and their eventual disintegration. none of these problems would arise if we were to build a true europe of sovereign nations, cooperating in the fields of their choice and for their mutual benefit.

in writing. there is a lot of talk about 'capacity for integration' in mr brok's report on the enlargement strategy, which is only intended to satisfy the interests and appetites for power of brussels. the report says that this 'capacity' should not be confused with 'the public perception of the impact of further enlargements'. you're wrong. firstly, because it is the citizens of the member states who are at the forefront of the economic and social consequences of enlargement and who therefore deserve to be heard. secondly, because they are the ones who will ultimately decide on these accessions. in france, for example, a referendum will be compulsory for any accession after croatia's. this is the "gift" that a defeated chirac has given us in an attempt to avoid a "no" vote on the european constitution. i also regret that the question of the geographical boundaries of europe and the definition of its common identity is never raised. it would be a good way of saying that turkey is a large country, but it is essentially, geographically, culturally, historically, demographically, an asian country. and that would put an end to the humiliating charade that these accession negotiations have become for her.
